agree.reason: A quick reader comes away with a clear, believable picture: he works an unsupervised 3 a.m. shift reliably and is already using data to catch disease, so most readers would rate him well, though nothing makes him stand out sharply from 150 applicants.

honest.reason: The claims stay within the brief, but 'seriously ill' makes 'got sick' a little stronger, and the letter quietly leaves out that he gave only two days' notice before leaving.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts are stated as given and never turned into stronger figures: about 780 scheduled shifts with 2 missed is over 99.7% attendance, and the value of catching nine mastitis cases is described but not estimated.

right_comparison.reason: Saying he is 'already doing the kind of work your program teaches' hints at a comparison with other applicants, but the letter never sets him against typical entrants or other workers the manager has supervised.

qualification.reason: The written-English caveat leans on 'taking a night class' without a start date, level, completion date or any sign of progress the committee could check.

objections.reason: The two likely doubts, whether he will stay the full two years and whether his written English can handle coursework, are raised directly and answered with the fact that he came back and with the night class, though the English answer is thin.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted one-page reference letter from the farm manager, of the length requested, with placeholders for details still to fill in.
